sections.overview: This small land snail survives in a few cool, moist refuges in the Driftless Area of the upper Midwest, principally in northeastern Iowa and nearby parts of Illinois.
sections.identification: It is a tiny discoid snail, about 5–8 mm across in the Iowa State University research account; the common name refers to its association with the Pleistocene fauna of the region.
sections.habitat: It lives in leaf litter on shaded, cool, moist algific talus slopes, where air cooled by underground ice emerges through openings in the slope.
sections.diet: The Iowa Pleistocene snail uses leaf litter, which provides both food and cover; the consulted species accounts do not define a more specific diet.
sections.behavior: The habitat remains below 10°C in summer and above −10°C in winter, according to the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service.
sections.reproduction: The reproductive mode is not established in the reviewed conservation account; self-fertilization is mentioned only as a possibility inferred from some related land snails.
sections.ecology: These fragile cold-air slope systems support a relict snail population; changes to the slope’s ice and moisture balance could remove the microclimate on which it depends.
sections.conservation: It has been federally listed as Endangered in the United States since 1978; threats include climate change, logging, quarrying, road work, sinkhole alteration, contamination and trampling.
